prompts.text: What's a funny way our group could welcome somebody who has just moved to the city?
Tell us about a new acquaintance who made a lasting impression at an ordinary event.
An introduction through a shared hobby or a casual meal with mutual friends?
We're hosting an event where everyone knows exactly one person. How do we stop people splitting into pairs?
The quietest newcomer may have the most interesting story once the right topic comes up.
A good host doesn't make a newcomer explain why they're shy.
What first-meeting question tells you something more interesting than someone's job?
Recall joining a conversation halfway through and unexpectedly feeling included.
A guest has travelled far to meet the group but knows none of our traditions. What could we do differently?
Invite a new person to help choose the music or ask them to pick the first game?
What's the funniest form of affection you've seen between two close friends?
Tell us about people who greet each other in an unusual way for a perfectly ordinary reason.
A friendship expressed through teasing or one expressed through thoughtful little surprises?
Two friends compete to give each other the most impractical handmade gifts. What prize should their audience award?
People often communicate closeness through personal routines that outsiders don't notice.
A friendship can be affectionate without everybody expressing it in the same way.
Who taught you that kindness can look different from what you expected?
Recall somebody showing care through a practical action rather than a conversation.
We must write a playful appreciation note for each person at the table. What detail would you include?
A funny compliment that still feels sincere or a straightforward thank-you for something specific?
Which relationship milestone do you think deserves a more entertaining celebration?
Recall somebody celebrating their first year in a new city with the friends who helped them settle.
Mark friendship anniversaries with a shared photo or a new activity each time?
Two members of our group celebrate separate achievements on the same day. How do we honour both?
People often remember the friends who witnessed a milestone as clearly as the achievement itself.
You don't have to throw a party for an accomplishment to feel celebrated.
What's a small personal achievement you'd be happy for our group to recognise?
Describe receiving unexpected congratulations from someone you didn't realise had been following your progress.
We organise a mini awards night where every prize must honour an ordinary quality. What categories are on the list?
A heartfelt toast from friends or a scrapbook full of amusing shared memories?
What's an embarrassing but harmless relationship lesson you learnt from a group game?
Tell us about accidentally teaming up with someone who turned out to be a perfect collaborator.
Partner with your closest friend or someone whose strengths are the opposite of yours?
Our group has to build something together from recycled materials. How should we assign roles?
Trust often grows fastest when people work through an unexpected inconvenience together.
A helpful teammate is someone who can admit when another person has a better idea.
Which friend would you ask to teach the group a skill they've never demonstrated before?
Recall a time a small group project revealed a friend's hidden patience.
We split into teams for a challenge, but one person feels overlooked. What would be a fair way to rebalance?
Solve a mystery cooperatively or race in pairs to complete simple tasks?
What's a surprisingly good question to ask friends who've been together as a couple for years?
Tell us about watching two people cooperate in a way that made everyone smile.
A couple that finishes each other's sentences or one that lovingly disagrees on everything?
A pair asks us to help plan an anniversary that suits both their personalities. How would we find a compromise?
A couple's shared humour is often a little different from either person's humour with friends.
Friends can support a relationship without acting like its unofficial committee.
What's a playful way to make someone's new partner feel welcome without overwhelming them?
Recall seeing a friend become happier through a relationship while staying recognisably themselves.
Our group plans a double date and everybody has different preferences. What planning question comes first?
A casual picnic for two couples or a cooperative activity that gives everyone something to do?
What's one social habit that shows someone has considered other people's time?
Describe a friend making a complicated group arrangement easier with one thoughtful decision.
Invite people with clear details or make an open-ended plan and decide together?
One friend regularly arrives with extra guests and nobody wants to embarrass them. How should we discuss it?
Respect can be expressed through small logistical choices as much as through words.
An invitation should never be treated like an obligation to attend.
What makes it easiest for you to decline a gathering while keeping the friendship comfortable?
Recall somebody gracefully accepting a last-minute change you couldn't avoid.
We plan a group outing but a friend has accessibility needs nobody considered. What's our next step?
Set a fixed end time for a gathering or agree that people can leave without explanation?
What misunderstanding between friends would be funny to reenact once everyone has made peace?
Tell us about an argument that turned out to be about two different definitions of the same word.
Talk through a misunderstanding during a short walk or over a quiet meal?
Two friends think the other deliberately ignored their message, but both phones had failed. How would the reveal go?
A small misunderstanding can grow when everyone waits for the other person to speak first.
Winning an argument rarely matters as much as understanding what the other person intended.
What's a lighthearted way to restart a conversation after an awkward pause?
Recall a friend admitting they were wrong without turning the moment into a performance.
We decide to write an apology using only clear, ordinary language. What should we leave out?
Resolve a minor disagreement promptly or take a quiet break before discussing it?
Which relationship advice from a film sounds brilliant until you imagine it in everyday life?
Tell us about a fictional friendship that reminded you of people in our group.
Watch a heartwarming film about friendship or a comedy about an unlikely group?
We cast each person here as a character in a fictional family sitcom. Who gets the unexpectedly wise role?
Stories about friendship are often more convincing when they include disagreements and repair.
A charming fictional gesture isn't necessarily a good idea to copy in real life.
What's a movie friendship you'd like to discuss with people who saw it differently?
Recall a book character whose loyalty reminded you of somebody you know.
Our group must invent a plot about strangers who become friends while stranded at a festival. What's the twist?
A mystery where old friends solve a problem together or a comedy about awkward first meetings?
What's a social rule your younger self would be surprised you no longer follow?
Describe a change in your friendships that initially felt strange but became healthy.
Keep an old group tradition or allow newcomers to reshape it over time?
Our circle is growing and one person worries they'll be forgotten. What's a practical way to include everyone?
People sometimes need different kinds of friendship at different points in their lives.
Growing apart doesn't automatically mean anybody did something wrong.
What positive change in someone you know took time for the rest of the group to notice?
Recall reconnecting with an old friend and finding your conversations had matured.
The people in this room meet again in ten years. Which shared value would you hope is unchanged?
Revive an old friendship with a simple hello or make space for a new connection?
Which unexpected friendship has reminded you not to judge people by first impressions?
Tell us about meeting somebody through an entirely different social circle and finding unexpected common ground.
Ask each person what they're learning lately or what they're looking forward to next month?
We create a group tradition where each person chooses a different guest to join us once. What keeps it welcoming?
A group becomes richer when people are free to introduce interests the others haven't tried.
Strong friendships leave room for one person to change without everyone feeling abandoned.
What would you like people you care about to feel after spending time with this group?
Recall a moment when a person's friendliness changed the atmosphere of an entire gathering.
We're putting together a cheerful farewell for a friend relocating overseas. What's one memory worth highlighting?
A group photo with everybody sharing one wish or individual notes that the friend can read later?
